title: How a Naked Mole-Rat Queen's Scent Keeps the Peace
summary:
Naked mole-rats work together in colonies, but they can also fight fiercely. Scientists recently found that a queen keeps her colony calm with a special scent.

In a colony, some mole-rats look for food and others care for the young. Only the queen has babies, and she stays in charge by keeping the others from mating. When a queen dies, high-ranking mole-rats begin mating and fight hard until one becomes the new queen.

Gary Lewin is a neuroscientist at the Max Delbrück Center in Berlin, Germany. He studies how naked mole-rats use their senses. He had found that they use scent to tell mole-rats from other colonies apart, and he wondered whether odors matter inside a colony too. His team found one chemical made only by queens. It is called isopropyl myristate. It seems to smell very strong to the animals, because it sets off activity in the part of the brain that processes smells.

To test it, the team removed a queen from her colony. Then they applied the chemical to the colony every day for three months. "In the entire three months, there was no fighting," Lewin said, and there was no mating. When the researchers stopped adding the scent, the mole-rats began to fight, and within a few weeks a new queen emerged.

In another test, pairs of males and females were separated from the colony. After four weeks, no female exposed to the scent had mated. Five of six females not exposed were pregnant. Blood tests showed the chemical changes hormones in females, lowering progesterone and raising prolactin.

The queen makes the chemical only when she is pregnant or preparing to be. The team shared its findings on July 15 in the journal Nature.
why_it_matters: The study shows how a single chemical can shape the behavior of a whole animal group, which helps scientists learn how animal societies keep order.

options: They hide food for the whole colony
They sing loudly to the other mole-rats
They release a scent that keeps the colony calm
They build new tunnels all alone

Moved the colony to a brand new lab
